title: The Spotlight on the Tepuis: Cleft Sentences

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know cleft sentences from B2 Unit 1 (*Lo que ... fue ...* and *Fue ... quien / donde / cuando*). They split one idea in two so that the piece you want to stress lands in the spotlight. The tepuis give you plenty to spotlight: what makes them special, where something is, who wrote about them.

sections.title: Three ways to put the spotlight on one idea
rows: Lo que hace únicos a los tepuyes es su aislamiento.
*lo que* + verb + *ser*: what makes the tepuis unique is their isolation
Es en el Auyantepuy donde empieza el Salto Ángel.
*es/fue* + place + *donde*: it is on the Auyantepuy that the Angel Falls begin
Fue Conan Doyle quien escribió una novela sobre una meseta aislada.
*fue* + person + *quien*: it was Conan Doyle who wrote a novel about an isolated plateau

items.spanish: Lo que hace únicos a los tepuyes es su aislamiento.
items.english: What makes the tepuis unique is their isolation.

items.spanish: Es en el Auyantepuy donde empieza el Salto Ángel.
items.english: It is on the Auyantepuy that the Angel Falls begin.

items.spanish: Fue en 1912 cuando Conan Doyle publicó «El mundo perdido».
items.english: It was in 1912 that Conan Doyle published The Lost World.

items.spanish: Lo que preocupa a las comunidades es el mercurio de la minería ilegal.
items.english: What worries the communities is the mercury from illegal mining.

sections.content: Use a cleft sentence for the one idea you want the listener to remember, not in every sentence. The tense of *ser* follows the other verb (*lo que preocupa es*, *fue en 1912 cuando*), and the spotlighted piece keeps its preposition: *es en el Auyantepuy donde*.
